[NOTE TO TRANSLATORS]notes: The entries marked as [NOTE TO TRANSLATORS] must be kept unchanged, in English, in all localization files.
[NOTE TO TRANSLATORS]updates: When new entries are added to the reference English localization file, they are also added to all the existing localization files for other languages with the mark [NEEDS TRANSLATION] prefixed to their key string and the original English text as their value string. This way, to keep a file up to date, translators just need to look for entries with that mark to know which entries haven't yet been translated (once the value is localized, the mark [NEEDS TRANSLATION] must be deleted from the key).
[NOTE TO TRANSLATORS]capitalization: In English, the capitalization of the entries follows two styles. Menu entries, option names, section names, button names and some others are capitalized as titles following the Chicago Manual of Style for headlines (for example: 'Go to First', 'Open with'). Modal logs, options inside selects, tooltips... use sentence capitalization (for example: 'Couldn't open the RAR file.'). This may not be valid or look natural in other languages (like Spanish) so, if you have doubts, do not just copy the English formatting, always use a capitalization style that is correct and standard for the target language.
